title: Draft: Taskfold fold timing, cache breakpoints, limits and debug mode

goals.text: A committed draft in .project/drafts/ proposes fold timing modes, report limits, routing fix, row accounting fix and debug mode.
The stable-breakpoint idea and provider awareness are verified against provider docs, Pi source and a simulation on real sessions, with evidence stored next to the draft.

report.outcome: Worktree .pi/worktrees/fold-timing-draft on docs/fold-timing-draft (from origin/feat/pi-native 40efb93). Existing sim (.project/analyses/fold-representations/harness/sim.py) models breakpoint caches but folds a task at the very request after it finishes, where the record is the last message; the shipped planner forbids that and folds one step later. So the sim never exercised span length or the one-step delay, and its 'eager is free' result does not transfer.
decisions: New draft DRAFT-fold-timing rather than revising DRAFT-taskfold-reliability - that one covers budget floor and protocol enforcement, a different undecided topic.
Reuse sim.py by copying it into the draft's evidence and extending it - the analysis' copy stays as its own evidence.
open: Host is pig (Go); breakpoint placement must be read from /mnt/Projects/furbyhaxx/pig, not pi-ai.

acceptanceCriteria.text: Worktree exists; existing drafts and the sim harness are known.

report.outcome: Cache semantics verified for Anthropic and OpenAI from vendor docs, breakpoint placement read from pig source, and Taskfold's rule confirmed to be provider-blind. Both major providers write entries only at breakpoints and look back about 20 positions, so a fold is cheap only if an entry exists at an unchanged position just before it.

subtasks.title: Anthropic: breakpoints, lookback, TTL, pricing from current docs

report.outcome: Anthropic prompt-caching docs (fetched 2026-11-10, copy at ~/.cache/pi-searxng/output/970a088ab1731c7f25a8.md): an entry is written only at a breakpoint; a read walks back at most 20 positions per breakpoint (the breakpoint counts) and finds prior writes, not stable content; runs of consecutive tool_use or tool_result blocks count as one position; up to 4 breakpoints; a hit refreshes the TTL. The docs recommend a second breakpoint when the last write falls outside the window.
decisions: Cost weights must be per model in the simulation - the analysis used 0.1/1.25 for all.
Prices: writes 1.25x (5 min) or 2x (1 h); reads 0.1x, but 0.05x on Sonnet 5.5 and Opus 5.5, 0.025x on Fable/Mythos 5.1+.

acceptanceCriteria.text: Lookback, entry creation, max breakpoints, TTL refresh and write prices quoted from the vendor docs.

subtasks.title: OpenAI and other providers: automatic prefix caching rules

report.outcome: OpenAI docs (KB capture 2026-11-04, ai-context-management/evidence/raw/harness/codex/api-prompt-caching.md): GPT-5.6+ also writes entries only at breakpoints; implicit mode puts one at the latest eligible message and looks up that plus up to 20 earlier eligible message endings; up to 4 writes per request; writes 1.25x (30 min) or 2.5x (12 h), reads 0.1x (0.05x for GPT-6.1 Sol/Terra). Earlier models cache at fixed token intervals with no write charge. DeepSeek persists prefix units at request ends, detected common prefixes and fixed intervals.
decisions: Three cache families for the planner: breakpoint+block lookback (Anthropic), breakpoint+message lookback (OpenAI GPT-5.6+), prefix-unit/interval (older OpenAI, DeepSeek, unknown).
open: The openai-codex (ChatGPT subscription) backend may differ from the public API docs; not verified.
No documented rule found for synthetic, xai, openrouter-routed or Gemini models in this pass.

acceptanceCriteria.text: Caching rule stated per provider family used in the sessions, with source.

subtasks.title: Pi: where breakpoints are placed and whether an extension can add one

report.outcome: pig (3dbc68a70) ai/anthropic.go places cache_control on every system block (1483; two blocks with an OAuth token, 1480), the last tool (867) and the last block of the final user message (470-487). That is 3 breakpoints with an API key and all 4 with OAuth, which the 'claude' provider uses. Extensions can rewrite the wire payload: pig-auth-plus already edits cache_control there (internal/hooks/hooks.go:46-119).
decisions: An extra breakpoint is feasible through before_provider_request; under OAuth it must replace the identity-block breakpoint, which is redundant with the system prompt's.
open: Not tested live: whether moving a cache_control marker alone changes the prefix hash (worst case one extra miss).
OpenAI explicit breakpoints (prompt_cache_breakpoint) are not emitted by pig today; only prompt_cache_key/retention.

acceptanceCriteria.text: Breakpoint placement located in pi-ai source per provider adapter.
Feasibility of an extension-placed breakpoint stated with the hook used.

subtasks.title: Taskfold: provider awareness of the deep rule and calibration units

report.outcome: The deep rule (taskfold.ts:743-745) has no provider or model input: one constant CACHE_LOOKBACK = 20, counted in Accordion blocks before the fold. recordTokens is compared through host.countTokens, which is calibrated (core/conductor/liveHost.ts:225). The calibration multiplier still absorbs tool-schema overhead (comment at extension/accordion.ts:2829-2831). SPEC-0002's leafForm 'bracket' option is specified but not implemented (no occurrence in any .ts file).
decisions: Treat k as content-dependent, not a constant: caps on agent-written text should be checked in characters or raw estimate, not calibrated tokens.
open: k for the audited session is inferred (~2.7 from widget sizes vs chars/4), not read from a log.

acceptanceCriteria.text: Stated whether the deep rule and recordTokens check depend on provider or calibration, with line references.

tasks.title: Simulate fold timing on real sessions

report.outcome: Simulator written, validated against real receipts and run on three sessions: folding every finished task one step after it closes is 19-30% cheaper than the shipped rule, and anchoring the cache at the fold boundary adds 7-14%.

subtasks.title: Understand and reuse the existing sim harness

report.outcome: sim.py replays a real Pi session per request with cache models lcp, bp and stable, but folds a task at the first request after its closing result, has no TTL, fixed 0.1/1.25 weights, and drops batched complete+start spans as crossing. timing_sim.py written and runs on the audited session (68 finished spans, 0 crossing).
decisions: New simulator .project/drafts/fold-timing/evidence/timing_sim.py instead of patching sim.py: it adds timestamps (TTL), block-counted lookback, the one-step fold delay, real receipts for validation and per-model weights.
Draft is a directory artifact: .project/drafts/fold-timing/README.md plus evidence/.

acceptanceCriteria.text: Know its inputs, cache models and whether it takes a real session.

subtasks.title: Validate the cache model against the audited session's real receipts

report.outcome: Validated on the audited session (now 1,510 requests): simulated shipped policy gives mean input 156k, peak 217.6k, read 231.5M, write 4.45M and 30 fold events, against real mean 164k, read 242.7M, write 5.39M and 25 shrinks from ~217k. Fit: S=35.7k, k=1.93. Output in evidence/validate-plan0029.txt.
decisions: Fit S and k per session on the requests before its first real fold; all policies share them.
open: The simulator has no floor, untracked folding, held blocks or user-message verdicts, and folds spans whole.

acceptanceCriteria.text: Simulated read/write for the as-run policy compared with the recorded usage.

subtasks.title: Compare pressure, lazy, eager and eager with frontier breakpoint

report.outcome: Three sessions simulated (evidence/modes-*.txt). Cost at Sonnet 5.5 read 0.05 / 1 h write 2.0, in M weighted tokens, shipped -> eager -> eager+frontier breakpoint -> eager+bracket tail: PLAN-0029 20.48 -> 14.41 -> 13.46 -> 13.48; auth-plus 25.40 -> 20.57 -> 18.26 -> 19.19; nukular-1106 16.41 -> 13.14 -> 11.30 -> 12.53. Eager saves 19-30%; a frontier breakpoint a further 7-14%; the bracket tail recovers 33-100% of that without payload rewriting. Mean input stays 103k-177k because open leaf tasks are large. Same ranking under OpenAI and prefix-cache profiles.
decisions: Recommend eager as default with the bracket tail first; the frontier breakpoint is an Anthropic-only second step.
Other two sessions ran on other models and budgets, so their rows are what-ifs at a 272k budget, not reproductions.

acceptanceCriteria.text: Weighted cost per mode for at least the audited session, for Anthropic and prefix-cache pricing.
